clue.text: Prince to name a dance

parts.note: Charles is the name of a well-known British prince
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal is asked to put a name to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s jazz-age ballroom step.

clue.text: He'sgotacheek!

parts.note: read as 'He's got a cheek!': both a man (a fellow) and the word for a jaw or cheek, as in chops

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed run together; it reads 'He's got a cheek!'. The word means a fellow, and also, in old usage, the jaw or cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is informally a man, and the same word in older English names the jaw or cheek.

clue.text: Slender types from wild Caith ness

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the place name run riot and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Lean people come from the untamed far north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits Caithness, a county in the far north of Scotland, in two; its nine letters, rearranged as 'wild' signals, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In old body-type classification, asthenic people have a thin, narrow, lightly built physique.

clue.text: Immature life-style of Pasternak's novel heroine about five

indicators.note: about means the heroine's name goes round the next piece

parts.note: Lara is the heroine of Pasternak's novel Doctor Zhivago
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A youthful way of life recalls the heroine of Doctor Zhivago.
explanation.walkthrough: Lara of Doctor Zhivago is wrapped 'about' the Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's grub stage is its immature form of life before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Perceived the digs unearthed

indicators.note: unearthed suggests the letters are dug up and turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: An archaeologist noticed the excavation sites being uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen or noticed has been perceived by the eye.

clue.text: Surface rock cut or shaped by work

indicators.note: shaped says the letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Stone at the surface has been cut or carved by labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by work' reads as how the rock was shaped, but 'work' supplies the musical opus abbreviation; 'shaped' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock that pokes up through the soil is exposed surface rock.

clue.text: A follower got up for a mess of porridge

parts.note: B comes after A in the alphabet, so it is A's follower
rose means got up, as from bed

explanation.surface: Someone rose early to make a bowl of porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' here is an old word for a dish of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Brose is a Scottish dish of oatmeal stirred with boiling water, a kind of porridge.

clue.text: Leasing or releasing, maybe

definitions.meaning: freeing something, such as a prisoner or a seam

explanation.definitionFit: Renting a flat to tenants and freeing an animal from a pen are both described by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Tender no longer? Not to worry

definitions.meaning: having no more tending to do, free of looking after anyone

explanation.definitionFit: Someone free of all concern has nothing to look after and nothing to fret about.

clue.text: Moving stairway

parts.note: 'Moving' is the meaning, an adjective for up and about, and the letters of 'stair' are moved around to show it

explanation.surface: An escalator, a moving staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an escalator; the word meant is 'moving' in the sense of up and stirring, made by moving the letters of STAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and stirring, as a household early in the morning, means being in motion.

clue.text: Moves around to eject a seaman

definitions.meaning: read as '...', AB being an able seaman

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels widely circulates; and putting an able seaman outside is getting him out.

clue.text: Windy inhabitant of the Eastern Mediterranean

definitions.text: Windy inhabitant of the Eastern Mediterranean

parts.words: Windy inhabitant of the Eastern Mediterranean
parts.note: a person from the eastern Mediterranean coast shares a name with a strong easterly wind of that region

explanation.surface: A long-winded resident of the Near East.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Levant shares a name with the strong easterly wind that blows through the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Fragrant substance of Oriental crushed lime

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east, so Oriental

indicators.note: crushed suggests the fruit is squashed and its letters reshaped

explanation.surface: An aromatic made from a pressed Eastern citrus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental' is the usual crossword signal for east; 'crushed' signals the anagram of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: One in the class of two masters

definitions.text: One in the class of two masters

parts.words: One in the class of two masters
parts.note: not a pupil taught by two teachers but a ship in the class of vessels with two masts

explanation.surface: A pupil taught by a pair of schoolmasters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a two-masted sailing vessel, square-rigged on the foremast.

clue.text: Was predominant as a rule

parts.note: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually' but means by holding royal rule

explanation.surface: Something generally prevailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who ruled held sway, and to prevail is to hold sway.

clue.text: Original stage turn, perhaps

parts.note: fresh means new and unusual, and a turn on stage is a performance piece

explanation.surface: A fresh routine on the variety stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh variety performance is a new piece put on by a performer.

clue.text: Topping Persian fairy to scold

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology
to wig is an old verb meaning to scold

explanation.surface: An excellent Persian sprite tells someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like 'excellent' but means something worn on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig worn on the head is a covering for its top, so a hairpiece is a topping.

clue.text: Tipsy on the rig?

parts.note: drunk, and on an oil rig a borehole might be greased in a literal sense

explanation.surface: Drunk while working offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for drunk, while on an oil platform the bore could be literally lubricated.

clue.text: Domestic appliance wayward son gave

indicators.note: wayward suggests the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: A difficult boy gave away a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooker heated by mains fuel is a household appliance.

clue.text: Soothing drug never mixed in taking

indicators.note: taking means the mixed word takes the next piece inside it
mixed says the letters of 'never' are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A calming medicine is never blended with anything you take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' makes NERVE from 'never', and 'taking' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that calms the nerves, a sedative.

clue.text: Where to get abuse left and right in recalling Wroclaw's German name

indicators.note: recalling, read as re-calling, says the letters are called up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A Polish city is where one hears insults from all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' rearranges ABUSE with L and R; Wroclaw in Poland was a German city until 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Before 1945 the Polish city of Wroclaw was German and bore this name.

clue.text: Portable equipment for a pert female

definitions.meaning: luggage and kit carried on a journey
an old word for a cheeky young woman

explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is carried kit, and the same word was once slang for a saucy girl.

clue.text: Post lately discovered by the Spanish

parts.note: something lately found is new
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Mail recently found by people in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests mail but means an upright at a staircase's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the upright post supporting a staircase handrail.

clue.text: Owned to revealing Odin's counterpart

indicators.note: revealing suggests the letters are laid open and shown in a different order

explanation.surface: A confession reveals something about a Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon form of the Norse chief god.

clue.text: Lively dance producing spectacles in drag of a sort

indicators.note: of a sort says the letters form a version of themselves in a new order

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: A dance performed by people in drag wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: OO (spectacles), IN and DRAG are mixed 'of a sort' into the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively old French dance for couples.

clue.text: Preliminary version silly but about right

indicators.note: about says the silly word goes round the next piece

parts.note: daft means silly

explanation.surface: A first version is foolish but nearly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough first write-up is a preliminary version to be revised.

clue.text: Cautious of what could go awry

indicators.note: what could go suggests the letters of 'awry' could go into another order

explanation.surface: Careful about things that might go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being on guard and careful.

clue.text: Part of SE Asia formed by party within the People's Republic

parts.note: in means within
a do is a party
China is the People's Republic

explanation.surface: A party is held inside China.
explanation.definitionFit: The French colonial region of Southeast Asia took this name.

clue.text: Everyone round a Scottish burgh

parts.note: all means everyone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: People gather around a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the Forth in central Scotland.

clue.text: High-flier found in Northern England

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soaring bird spotted in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a bird that soars high.

clue.text: The rest of creation

parts.note: not everything else in the world but the time of rest in the Genesis account

explanation.surface: Everything else in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis God rested on the final day after six days making the world.
